items.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: "But the whole thing, Monk, is it’s got to swing."

ctx.x: And physical in movement but also I think that must mean something beyond that you move around stage.

Yeah, right, yeah, yeah. It’s more than that, it’s more than that. But it’s almost to the point where I’m conducting you know, because the guys tell me, “I saw that shoulder moving.” I say, “You did, yeah.” So whatever the shoulder means, and I’m singing, whatever they get out of that shoulder, fine you know. If it’s going to bring us in and it’s going to make us tighter, fine. I don’t know what it means. They say, “Well when you’re singing you shake your leg” you know. I say, “Well I’m keeping time.” No there’s…

And the part that you were talking about doing, the clapping thing, which I think I probably will steal that by the way because — it’s funny when people start clapping on one and three, I sometimes don’t know how to deal with that. So I love your — ask them which feels better. Did you have someone when you were a young person helping you learn?
